scenarios.basis: M2 average annual growth 1394-12→1397-12, the slowest Esfand-to-Esfand three years since 1390

trend.note: The dollar's own trend: the mean monthly change of its log monthly average since 1390-10, carried forward from the latest close. It is the benchmark the M2 paths are measured against, and it is not a forecast either.

band.note: The band is the 5th–95th percentile of the M2-paced path's past errors (month-end close, origins from 1394-01, at least 12 per horizon, widened so it never narrows). In the backtest, the same rule, applied at each past date to the errors known by then, held the actual price 80% of the time at 1–12 months, 86% at 13–24 months and 90% at 24 months (79 origins, about 3 independent outcomes). At 1–12 months and 13–24 months that is less often than the 90% its quantiles span: later errors fell outside the range of the errors before them more often than that implies, and the future can surprise by more than the past did. The band is not centred on the path: the median 12-month error was +0.021, so the dollar ended above the path more often than not.

backtest.verdict: In the backtest (origins from 1394-01 with outcomes known by 1405-06, month-end close), the dollar growing at M2's pace beat “no change” at every horizon tested (3, 6, 12 and 24 months, one-sided p ≤ 0.002); against the dollar's own trend it was not measurably better at any horizon tested (RMSE 0.8% to 6.0% lower, one-sided p = 0.186 to 0.303). The trend alone beat “no change” at every horizon tested (3, 6, 12 and 24 months, one-sided p ≤ 0.004).
backtest.note: Root mean square of log errors (0.10 is roughly a 10% miss). One-sided Diebold–Mariano tests with the Harvey–Leybourne–Newbold small-sample correction. Forecasts from consecutive months overlap, so the 114 origins scored at 24 months hold only about 5 independent outcomes.

lag_check.note: Rerun with each M2 month usable only 6 months after it ended -- later than any delay CBI is measured to have taken -- the dollar growing at M2's pace beat “no change” at every horizon tested (3, 6, 12 and 24 months, one-sided p ≤ 0.002); against the dollar's own trend it was not measurably better at any horizon tested (RMSE 0.3% to 5.9% lower, one-sided p = 0.315 to 0.382). Every horizon falls on the same side of p = 0.05 as at 3 months, so the conclusions do not rest on the 3-month assumption.

liquidity_dollar.note: Not a fair value. The liquidity dollar is a base month's dollar scaled by M2 growth since then, and the base month decides the answer: every month is a candidate and they disagree by a factor of several. In the research this level model also lost to the dollar's own trend as a forecast.

notes: Scenario paths, not forecasts: each line is where the dollar would be if, from the latest close, it grew as fast as M2 did over the stated span -- not a prediction, not a fair value and not a target. The backtest says, from its own numbers, how paths built this way did against the dollar's own trend.
Correlation is not causation: M2 and the dollar both rose with Iran's inflation, and the growth of one did not lead the other at any stable lag.
What the model cannot see: sanctions and oil revenue, war and politics, expectations, the multiple exchange rates, and the central bank's foreign-exchange interventions.

USD_IRT changes definition on 2026-10-11 (the splice register): before it, one daily close of TGJU's price_dollar_rl — the free-market CASH dollar in Tehran, published in rials and stored as toman; from it, the 24/7 USDT/toman market used as the free-market proxy, which carries its own stablecoin premium over cash dollars. A monthly figure, path or backtest error that spans that date mixes the two. It is not CBI's official or NIMA rate.

M2 is CBI's end-of-month stock in thousand billion rial (÷10 = همت). The backtest treats each month as usable 3 months after it ended and uses today's figure for it. CBI states no release date; its workbooks have arrived 21 to 164 days after the month ended, so for some origins 3 months is early, and backtest.lag_check reruns the comparison at 6. Of the figures it reads, no stored M2 month has been revised by a later CBI edition.
Base money is not used here: its 1399-12 redefinition breaks its growth, and it forecast no better than M2 in the research.

money.note: CBI states no release date. Its monthly workbooks have arrived 21 to 164 days after the month they describe (three weeks to five and a half months, measured from the workbooks' own last-saved times), often several at once. age_days is measured from the end of the newest stored month to today (Tehran); that month is called stale after 195 days, the longest lag plus one month, because until the next month is published the newest stored one is a month older than it.
